clues: This town sits on the south bank of a big river. Two small rivers join just upstream to form it.
Winters here are short and mild, but summers stretch on long, hot, and humid. On most summer days the heat climbs past 90 degrees.
In 1846, the state moved its capital here from an old town. Cotton farms had grown rich, and power had moved south.
In 1955, Rosa Parks would not give up her bus seat to a white man. She was put in jail, and a bus boycott that changed the land began.
The governor of Alabama works in this town. Its lawmakers meet here in the capitol, on a hill.
